inevitable_need: A hard wall between clients for our agents: each client engagement gets its own scoped context and permissions, so an agent working in client A's repo can never see client B's code, Slack or docs, plus a plain log of what the agent read and changed that I can hand to that client.
why_inevitable: Clients are starting to ask in procurement whether we use AI agents on their code and what data those agents can see. Once one of them makes it a contract clause, I either show isolation and a log or I lose the engagement.
must_have: Per-client isolation that holds up: separate stores and credentials per engagement, not a tag on shared data
Runs on our own infrastructure or the client's, set up in an afternoon with Docker
Works with the agents we already use (Claude Code, Cursor) through MCP, with no lock-in to a new chat UI
deal_breakers: Client code or Slack going through a vendor's hosted service, especially one still in preview
Per-seat pricing that costs more than the hours it would take us to build a rough version ourselves
Needing a dedicated person to keep it running or tune it
expected_provider: Probably my own team first, a vector DB and an MCP server per client wired up in a few weekends. Longer term I expect Anthropic or Cursor to ship workspace-level scoping and audit logs, which would make a separate tool redundant for a shop our size.
memoryworks_would_need: Make per-client isolation a first-class feature of the self-hosted MIT version, with one instance or namespace per client and an exportable log of what each agent was briefed on and did that I can give to the client. Then show it stopping an agent from repeating a real past incident on one of our repos. I'd pay a small flat support fee, not $20 a head.
